title: Mathematician and Claude release a Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis
summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, released a Lean library of about 17 million lines that he states proves the Riemann hypothesis and the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, developed with Claude. His accompanying note says he guided the argument from a toy setting while Claude supplied much of the technical work, including the √X length of a chain of theta lifts; the note's timeline runs from 6 October to 16 November 2026. A day after release, the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative certified that the library proves Mathlib's statement of the Riemann hypothesis and passes several independent proof checkers. No human-readable proof has been published, and Alpöge writes that he has not yet mastered parts of the argument.

evidence.tested: The Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative state that dozens of people reproduced compilation, that two comparison tools confirmed the proved theorem is exactly Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis statement, and that the exported proof passed Lean's kernel and several independent checkers, including formally verified ones.
evidence.unknown: No natural-language proof or peer-reviewed paper is available; the mathematical ideas have not yet been explained or checked by independent mathematicians. The exact Claude model version is not stated in the author's note.
evidence.ai_role: Per the author, Claude carried out much of the technical development and the Lean formalization after he guided it to the setting analogous to a toy argument; he credits Claude with tens of such transfers, including the choice of chain length of theta lifts.

source_review.scope: Author's four-page note (alpo.ge/remark.pdf) and the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative statement; the Lean library itself not inspected
